# CGR-400..CGR-699 — `bevy_core_pipeline` minus `core_2d/**` / `core_3d/**`, entity by entity

Scope: everything in `bevy_core_pipeline` **except** `core_2d/**` and `core_3d/**` (owned by the
CGR-100..CGR-310 agent): `tonemapping/**`, `upscaling/**`, `blit/**`, `prepass/**`, `deferred/**`,
`skybox/**`, `oit/**`, `experimental/mip_generation/**`, `fullscreen_material.rs`,
`fullscreen_vertex_shader/**`, `lib.rs`.

Bevy source pinned at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/`, tag `v0.18.0`, commit
`5f8270f2e049f90139a503d1e930070d926f9427`. All line numbers are true file line numbers as reported
by the read tool (the brief's parenthesised sizes equal `Measure-Object -Line`, which counts
non-blank lines only; e.g. `tonemapping/mod.rs` is 456 real lines, not 419).

**Row granularity convention.** One row per Bevy entity, in Bevy's declaration order. Where a
group of plain data members shares one status they are enumerated in a single `field` row with each
member's line number (e.g. `CGR-401`); a member gets its own row when its status is independent.
`method` rows carry the verdict where the body cannot diverge from Bevy's shape; a `def` row is
added when the body is the thing that needs checking (pipeline construction, bind-group layouts,
buffer/uniform layouts, specialization keys and shader defs, node ordering, texture allocation,
clear/load/store decisions, LUT handling, dispatch arithmetic).

**Node-label convention (brief, verified).** In the pinned source `#[derive(RenderLabel)]` emits
only `dyn_clone`; label identity is `Interned<dyn RenderLabel>` = (type, value) and there is no
label string. Rows therefore compare the label *type*/variant names, and strings such as
`CopyDeferredLightingIdNode::NAME` are not required counterparts.

**Shader convention.** Epix keeps shaders as embedded Slang string literals inside the
corresponding `.cpp`/`.hpp`. Slang-vs-WGSL is the recorded convention, not a mismatch; the compared
surface is binding indices/stages, entry-point names, arithmetic, and control flow.

**Epix counterparts.** `epix_engine/render/core_graph/**`; `epix_engine/render/render/**` where an
entity lives there (marked `PARENT: render`); `epix_engine/pbr/**` where a `bevy_pbr` consumer of a
core-pipeline entity matters (marked `PARENT: pbr`). `OIT` was absent from Epix and still has one row
per Bevy public entity rather than a deep analysis; the three entities the pbr mesh view layout needs
(`CGR-571`, `CGR-580`, `CGR-582`) were ported in batch 47, so the rest of that block stays 🚫.

3. *(CGR-542 ✅ fixed in `ac02885e` — the deferred query carries the override and both gates.)*
4. **CGR-571 / CGR-580 / CGR-582 ✅** ported in `4997243a`: `OrderIndependentTransparencySettings` (Bevy's two fields and defaults, also the shader's eight-byte uniform), `OIT_REQUIRED_STORAGE_BUFFERS = 2`, and `is_oit_supported` (both device facts as parameters, with Bevy's warning texts). The rest of OIT is still 🚫 — **CGR-572..CGR-579**, **CGR-581**, **CGR-583..CGR-593**: the `Component` impl and its `on_add` warning, `OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin`, `configure_depth_texture_usages`, `check_msaa`, `OitBuffers`, `init_oit_buffers`, the settings-offset component, `prepare_oit_buffers`, `OitResolvePlugin`, `OitResolveBindGroup`, `OitResolvePipeline`, `OitResolvePipelineId`/`Key`, `queue_`/`specialize_`/`prepare_oit_resolve_*`, `OitResolvePass`, `OitResolveNode`, and both shaders. `PARENT: pbr` already emits `OIT_ENABLED` and an `oit_mesh_pipeline` (`pbr/include/epix/pbr/mesh_pipeline.hpp`, locked by `cluster_tests.cpp:4290-4301`) with no layer buffers to write into, so that shader def is currently inert.
5. **CGR-489 / CGR-490 / CGR-496 / CGR-500** — 🚫 `DepthPrepassDoubleBuffer` and `DeferredPrepassDoubleBuffer` do not exist, and without them `ViewPrepassTextures::{previous_depth_view, previous_deferred_view}` have no source: no Epix view can read the previous frame's depth or deferred G-buffer.
6. **CGR-454** — 🚫 `approximate_inverse_tone_mapping` has no Epix counterpart; its only Bevy consumer is `bevy_pbr` transmission (`pbr_transmission.wgsl:14,78,188`). `PARENT: pbr`.
7. **CGR-446 / CGR-450** — 🚫 `convertNormalizedLog2ToOpenDomain` (dead in Bevy — never called) and `rgb_to_srgb_simple` (bloom re-declares its own copy) are the only two shared shader helpers Epix omits; no core-pipeline behaviour changes.
8. **CGR-637** — ⚠️ `DownsampleDepthNode` has no shadow-map pass: Bevy also downsamples each `OcclusionCullingSubviewEntities` light at `depth_texture_size` (:206-223), so shadow occlusion culling has no pyramid in Epix.
9. **CGR-521 / CGR-545** — ⚠️ `LatePrepassNode` and `LateDeferredGBufferPrepassNode` return immediately instead of running the early body when occlusion culling is on (no early/late bin split yet; C14-D2 / C15-D2). Required alignment: land the bin splitter, then remove both no-ops.

**Recorded intentional divergences (⚠️, rationale in the row):**

10. **CGR-404 / CGR-414 / CGR-456** — no `lut_bindings.wgsl` asset and no `TONEMAPPING_LUT_*_BINDING_INDEX` shader defs: the two LUT bindings are literal `[[vk::binding(3/4)]]` in `tonemapping.slang`. Same indices and stages.
11. **CGR-427 / CGR-428** — the LUTs are decoded by hand into `RGBA32Float` where Bevy keeps the KTX2's native, always-filterable format (REVIEW: on an adapter without 32-bit-float filtering the filterable 3D-texture LUT binding can fail validation; not verifiable read-only), and `lut_placeholder` exists but is never installed because there is no `tonemapping_luts`-off branch.
12. **CGR-410 / CGR-441** — `Tonemapping`'s variant order is rearranged to reproduce Bevy's `#[default]`, and `TONY_MC_MAPFACE_LUT_DIMS` is inlined as literals. Neither has a behavioural effect.
13. **CGR-511** — Epix-only `prepass_pipeline_targets`: the webgpu C++ target array cannot hold a hole, so an unwritten location becomes an `Undefined`-format target (documented, and covered by a skybox test).
14. **CGR-512 / CGR-513 / CGR-514** — `update_previous_view_data`, `prepare_previous_view_uniforms` and `ExtractComponent<PreviousViewData>` are Epix-only in `core_graph`; Bevy's equivalents live in `bevy_pbr`. `PARENT: pbr` must not define a second copy of either system.
15. **CGR-517 / CGR-539 / CGR-544** — `EarlyPrepassNode`'s query drops the optional skybox/previous-view items (looked up in the body instead), the deferred phase items and formats live in `core3d.hpp` rather than a `deferred` module, and `LateDeferredGBufferPrepassNode` is exposed as `Core3dNodes::LateDeferredPrepass` (Bevy's variant name).
16. **CGR-555** — `CopyDeferredLightingIdNode::NAME` has no string counterpart; label identity is the interned (type, value) pair (brief's label note).
17. **CGR-600 / CGR-601 / CGR-612 / CGR-622** — Skybox uniforms are derived in a render-world system instead of inside `ExtractComponent`, and the wasm `SIXTEEN_BYTE_ALIGNMENT` padding is unconditional in the C++ struct (same 80-byte layout).
18. **CGR-617** — `SkyboxPlugin` builds `SkyboxPrepassPipeline` and `PreviousViewUniforms` in one `RenderStartup` closure, because the dynamic buffer needs the device's `minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment`.
19. **CGR-632** — `MipGenerationPlugin` seeds its shader/specialization resources in `attach` and disables itself when the asset registry or server is absent.
20. **CGR-643** — every pyramid storage entry is `ReadWrite` where Bevy marks binding 6 `ReadWrite` and the rest `WriteOnly` (Slang/HLSL have no write-only storage declaration); the access mode is a superset.
21. **CGR-549** — ⛔ Bevy's `webgl && wasm32 && !webgpu` deferred-clear fallback is compiled out natively and has no counterpart; Epix implements the native clear-on-both-nodes behaviour.
22. **CGR-676 / CGR-681** — the `FullscreenMaterial` constraint set is spelled `ShaderWritable` instead of `WriteInto` with component-ness implicit, and `FullscreenMaterialLabel` is a `NodeLabel` subtype instead of a `type_name` wrapper.
23. Structural only, no behavioural consequence: **CGR-459** (`ambiguous_with_all`), **CGR-463** (a no-output-texture guard), **CGR-473** (`allow_ambiguous_resource`), **CGR-652** (max-mips clamped to ≥1 at a zero extent), **CGR-695 / CGR-699** (module surface and plugin list — the only omitted plugin is `OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin`, which is row 4 above).

# bevy_pbr `render/mesh.rs` — PBR mesh pipeline, keys, instance extraction and bind groups

Block `PBR-100`..`PBR-499`. One row per entity in `bevy_pbr/src/render/mesh.rs`
(3431 lines in the pinned tree, not 3143), plus the `mesh_bindings.rs` /
`mesh_view_bindings.rs` interfaces `mesh.rs` consumes, and — since the block boundary
over the remaining mesh files was lifted — the `prepass/prepass_bindings.rs` and
`light_probe/{environment_map,irradiance_volume}.rs` helpers the view layout adds
(`PBR-281`..`PBR-284`). `mesh.rs` contains **no**
`MeshPipelineViewLayouts`, `MeshPipelineViewLayout`, `MeshPipelinePreprocess` or
`preprocess`: in 0.18 those live in `mesh_view_bindings.rs` and
`gpu_preprocess.rs`, and only the parts `mesh.rs` owns appear here.

**Headline finding:** Epix ports `MeshPipelineKey`, the five blend/depth pass
arms, the shader-def derivation and the morph/skinning layout precedence — and
nothing else. `MeshPipeline`, `MeshRenderPlugin`, every extraction system, every
bind group, `SetMesh*BindGroup` and `DrawMesh` have no counterpart. Epix does have
a *complete* 2D analogue (`epix::sprite_render::Mesh2dPipeline` in
`mesh2d_pipeline.hpp`/`mesh2d_pipeline.cpp`), so the 3D gap is not an absence of
infrastructure — it is an unported pipeline.

## Summary

Counts: ✅ 205 · ❌ 8 · ⚠️ 17 · 🚫 1 · ⛔ 0 · REVIEW 1 (230 rows, `PBR-100`..`PBR-322` plus the `PRT-4`..`PRT-6` parent rows).
| PBR-895 | def | `ViewSpecializationItem` tests `Has<PerspectiveProjection>` and `Has<OrthographicProjection>` where Bevy reads one `Projection` enum, and this port already requires a `Projection` on every `Camera3d` | Bevy `mesh.rs:312-335` (one `Projection`); port `camera.hpp:433-435` (the requirement) against `mesh_view_key.hpp:116-126` (the query) | `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/mesh_view_key.hpp` | ✅ | **Batch 212: the real defect behind the batch-195 observation, found by the user correcting PRT-7.** `PRT-7` claimed `Camera3d` carries no `Projection`; it does - `Camera3d::register_required_components` registers one (`camera.hpp:433-435`), mirroring Bevy `#[require(Camera, Projection)]`, and this port `Camera` hook lists exactly Bevy own set. So the reason the mesh view key read the nonstandard case in a real app is here: the specialisation query asks for `PerspectiveProjection`/`OrthographicProjection` as separate components, and the requirement supplies `Projection`, which is a different thing in this port as it is in Bevy. **Fix owed:** read the port `Projection` kind in the query, as Bevy does, and correct the projection arm of `make_mesh_view_key` to take that kind. The example already demonstrates the bug and its workaround - it names `PerspectiveProjection` by hand, with a comment that is now wrong. **Batch 213: fixed and verified.** The query takes `const epix::camera::Projection&` - Bevy shape, and the port `Projection` is the same variant type over perspective, orthographic and custom - and the arm switches on the active alternative. **The root cause was a comment:** the header claimed this port carries the two projections as separate components, which is why the wrong query looked right; it is corrected. **The example workaround is deleted**, so the test is stronger than a fix alone - the key reads `perspective=true` with no projection named at all. The material-extract test that drives this system needed `Projection` on its spawned view too, and it failed *when run alone*, which is how the suite distinguished my regression from the known flake; the commit gate stopped the first attempt. | 

The 36 ❌ rows are overwhelmingly one fact seen from many angles: **Epix has no 3D mesh pipeline**.
`MeshPipeline`, `MeshRenderPlugin`, the view bind groups and every remaining render command in `mesh.rs`
are absent, and of the extraction stage only the GPU path's query, system and helper are ported —
`MeshExtractionSystems`, the CPU path, the motion-vector flag writer and `collect_meshes_for_gpu_building`
are not. What *is* ported — `MeshPipelineKey` and the view-layout key with every flag, shift and mask
bit-exact (now with Bevy's two compile-time layout assertions), the five pass arms with their blend and
depth-write rules, the shader-def derivation, the morph/skinning layout precedence, and the GPU instance
queues with the two extraction functions that fill them, the eight mesh bind group layouts, the view layout with every entry it names, the pipeline resource that holds it, every mesh shader module it loads but two, and the shared maths library it imports — is ported correctly, plus the three `PARENT: render` rows it found, which is why 187 rows are ✅.

The 9 ⚠️ rows are representation choices (`MainEntity` instead of `RetainedViewEntity`, `glm::mat4` for
`Affine3`, explicit tail padding for `ShaderType` rounding, an unenforced `NonMaxU32` invariant, two maps
plus a tag instead of an enum, one queue instead of `Parallel<…>`), the seven cargo-feature-gated shader
defs (PBR-244), one unwired-but-parity-correct primitive state (PBR-257), one pair of labels with no
descriptor to carry them (PBR-260), and one vertex-layout conversion that exists with its presence
derivation but has no caller yet (PBR-261). The four parameter-only capability fields that used to be
listed here (PBR-189..192) are aligned as of batch 52: `MeshPipeline` owns them.

## Not audited

- `mesh_view_bindings.rs` — **the layout half is audited and ported as of batch 50**: the layout keys (PBR-272..276), `MeshPipelineViewLayout` (`PBR-271`), `buffer_layout` (`PBR-297`), `layout_entries` (`PBR-298`), `MeshPipelineViewLayouts` (`PBR-299`) and `generate_view_layouts` (`PBR-300`). What remains is the runtime half — `MeshViewBindGroup` (`PBR-301`) and `prepare_mesh_view_bind_groups` (`PBR-302`) — which needs the device, the pipeline cache and runtime buffers that are not ported.
- `MeshLayouts`' per-entry layout builders (`mesh_bindings.rs:25-161`, `layout_entry::*`/`entry::*`) — **in scope as of this round**; rows PBR-266..270 record the interface `mesh.rs` calls and are the port's checklist.
- GPU preprocessing: `MeshPipelinePreprocess`, `preprocess`, `PreprocessPipelines`, `PreprocessBindGroups`, `IndirectParametersBuffers`. All of these live in `bevy_pbr/src/render/gpu_preprocess.rs` in 0.18, not in `mesh.rs`; `mesh.rs` only names `PreprocessPipelines`/`PreprocessBindGroups` in `DrawMesh`'s `Param`/`ViewQuery` (PBR-241).
- `bevy_pbr/src/prepass/prepass_bindings.rs` — **audited and ported as of batch 41** (`PBR-281`, `PBR-282`); the rest of `bevy_pbr/src/prepass/**` (`mod.rs`'s plugin, node and `PreviousGlobalTransform` update system, `prepass.rs`, `prepass_pipeline.rs`) is still unaudited, which is why `PreviousGlobalTransform` is recorded inside `PBR-154`'s row rather than as a row of its own.
- `bevy_pbr/src/light_probe/**` — only the two `get_bind_group_layout_entries` helpers the view layout calls are audited and ported (`PBR-283`, `PBR-284`, batch 43). The rest of the block (`mod.rs`'s plugin, extraction/preparation, `generate.rs`, the bindings constructors and the WGSL) is unaudited; `EnvironmentMapUniform`, `MAX_VIEW_LIGHT_PROBES` and `EnvironmentMapUniformBuffer` already existed in `pbr/light_probe.hpp` and are not claimed here.
- `bevy_pbr/src/decal/clustered.rs` — the four entities the view layout needs are audited and ported (`PBR-285`..`PBR-288`, batch 46): the GPU object, the decal cap, the usability check and the layout entries. The rest of the file (`ClusteredDecal` is already ported in `light_cluster.hpp`, but `extract_decals`, `prepare_decals`, `RenderClusteredDecals`, the bind group and the WGSL) is unaudited.
- `bevy_pbr/src/ssr/**` — only the three entities the view layout needs are audited and ported (`PBR-289`..`PBR-291`, batch 48): the settings component, its GPU uniform and the conversion between them, because binding 15 is unconditional. The rest of the block (`ScreenSpaceReflectionsPlugin`, the node, the pipeline and its specialization, the bind group and the WGSL) is unaudited.
- `bevy_pbr/src/atmosphere/**` — only the five shader-data entities the view layout needs are audited and ported (`PBR-292`..`PBR-296`, batch 49): the mode, the two settings forms and their conversion, the GPU atmosphere, and the buffer both go in, because binding 31 is a storage buffer of `AtmosphereData`. Everything that produces or consumes them (`Atmosphere` itself, `ScatteringMedium`, the LUT textures, the environment/render-sky nodes, the plugin and the WGSL) is unaudited.
- `bevy_pbr/src/render/skin.rs` (`SkinUniforms`, `MAX_JOINTS`, `skins_use_uniform_buffers`) and `render/morph.rs` (`MorphUniforms`, `MorphIndices`, `extract_morphs`, `prepare_morphs`) — separate files, separate blocks. Their absence in Epix is visible here only as a consequence (PBR-181, PBR-192, PBR-266), except for `MAX_JOINTS` and `skins_use_uniform_buffers`, which batch 38 ported into `pbr/skin.hpp` because the mesh layouts need them.
- `bevy_pbr/src/material.rs`'s `alpha_mode_pipeline_key`, `tonemapping_pipeline_key`, `screen_space_specular_transmission_pipeline_key` — owned by the material section. Epix keeps all three in `mesh_pipeline_key.hpp:529-588`; parity of values was verified incidentally and they match, but the rows belong to that block.
- `bevy_pbr/src/lightmap/mod.rs`, `material_bind_groups.rs`, `meshlet/*`, `deferred/*`, `oit/*`, `ssr/*`, `volumetric_fog/*` — only referenced where `mesh.rs` names them.
- `RenderPipelineDescriptor`, `SpecializedMeshPipeline`, `SpecializedMeshPipelines`, `BinnedRenderPhasePlugin`, `RenderSystems`, `NoIndirectDrawing`, `MeshAllocator`, `RenderMesh` — `PARENT: render`; only their interface shape is cited, no rows claimed.
- Nothing was built or run. Bit layouts were verified by reading the pinned declarations and Epix's own `static_assert`s/tests, not by execution.

Nothing consumes `Has<ExtractedAtmosphere>` yet, because the view specialisation system that reads it is `PBR-115`. A new four-test binary covers the earthlike numbers term for term and each arm numerics. Still absent: the GPU render asset, the sampler and the plugin. |
| PBR-887 | def | `ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusion` — the component and the pass it drives | `bevy_pbr/src/ssao/mod.rs` | `none` | 🚫 | Missing, with **no counterpart anywhere** in the port, and the pass it drives is a render-graph node - so this is a render-module item before it is a `pbr` one, and it gates `PBR-115`'s `HAS_SSAO` key bit the same way. Recorded here so the input list has a row to point at rather than a name. |
| PBR-888 | def | `ScatteringMedium` - the asset and its parts | `bevy_pbr/src/medium.rs:25-565` | `pbr/scattering_medium.hpp` | ⚠️ | **Batch 175: the data is ported, the GPU side is not.** Present: `Falloff` (linear/exponential/tent with Bevy formulas verbatim, plus `Sampled` standing in for Bevy `Curve` by decision), `PhaseFunction` data, `ScatteringTerm`, `ScatteringMedium` with its builders and `earthlike`, and a device-free test binary. Absent: `GpuScatteringMedium`, the medium sampler, and `ScatteringMediumPlugin` with its `RenderAssetPlugin` and `RenderStartup` system. **Batch 176: the phase evaluator and the LUT data are in.** `PhaseFunction::sample` carries Bevy formulas verbatim - isotropic `0.25/pi`, Rayleigh `0.1875/pi * (1 + cos^2)`, Mie with the `denom^1.5` denominator - plus a `Sampled` arm interpolating over [-1, 1]. The two LUT data builders reproduce Bevy `prepare_asset`: a density LUT of `2 * falloff_resolution` vec4s (absorption then scattering) and a scattering LUT of `falloff_resolution * phase_resolution`, both sampling at **cell centres** `(i + 0.5) / resolution`, with the scattering LUT keeping Bevy index order exactly - falloff as the fast axis, phase as the slow one, `neg_l_dot_v = 2p - 1`. **And a fidelity bug of mine was caught by reading:** I had defaulted `PhaseFunction` to `Isotropic`, where Bevy `#[default]` is `Mie { asymmetry: 0.8 }`; the fix then exposed that my `isotropic()` factory had relied on the default, exactly the trap Bevy own `Default` sets. Still absent: the LUT textures and their upload, the sampler, `GpuScatteringMedium` as a render asset, and the plugin. **Batch 177: the LUT textures, the sampler and the device path are in - the row closes for the data and GPU halves.** `GpuScatteringMedium` carries the two textures and views plus the terms and resolutions, and `make_gpu_scattering_medium` builds them: density `falloff_resolution x 2`, scattering `falloff_resolution x phase_resolution`, both `Rgba32Float` and texture-binding only. Bevy uploads with `create_texture_with_data`, which this wrapper lacks, so the port creates the texture and uses `writeTexture` - the idiom `dummy_white_image.cpp` already follows. The sampler is linear on both filters and labelled, as Bevy creates it. A GPU test asserts the sizes, the format, that the terms travel with the LUTs, and that both calls complete on a real device. **Still absent:** `ScatteringMediumPlugin` - the asset registration, the `RenderAssetPlugin` and the `RenderStartup` sampler system - which is what makes any of this run in an app rather than in a test. **Batch 178: the plugin is in, and with it the row is complete except its wiring.** `ScatteringMediumPlugin::attach` registers the asset (`assets::app_register_asset<ScatteringMedium>` - the port spelling) and the render-asset pairing (`RenderAssetPlugin<GpuScatteringMedium>`, one template argument: the port pairs it with the source through the `RenderAsset` specialisation, and a second argument would be an ordering plugin), and adds `init_scattering_medium_sampler` to `RenderStartup`, which inserts the sampler. A `RenderAsset<GpuScatteringMedium>` specialisation carries Bevy `prepare_asset` with `Param` as the device and queue, and Bevy default `asset_usage` covering both worlds. **The plugin test is owed** - the factories have device-free coverage and the GPU path has a device test, but nothing asserts yet that adding the plugin registers the asset, the render asset and the sampler. **Batch 188: the plugin test is delivered for its two registrations, and the third is a harness limit.** The test asserts what `attach` does - `Assets<ScatteringMedium>` exists and the render-asset plugin pairs it with `GpuScatteringMedium` - and those two now have coverage. **The sampler stays uncovered:** the plugin puts it in a `RenderStartup` system, and running that schedule by hand - prepared and initialized, with deferred work applied, following exactly what `App::run` does before its first run - inserted nothing and logged **no validation error**, so the hand-run schedule does not reach the system in this harness. The test says that rather than asserting around it. **A third harness limit, then, in the same family as the others:** `App::run` does more than the harness can reproduce - `ready` runs only there, the render world `FrameCount` exists only from the second frame, and now a `RenderStartup` system is not reached by a hand-run schedule. |

# `bevy_light` lights, shadows, clusters, probes and fog — PBR light entity audit

Block `PBR-500`..`PBR-899`. One row per entity in `bevy_light/src/{lib,ambient_light,cascade,
directional_light,point_light,spot_light,probe,volumetric}.rs` and `bevy_light/src/cluster/{mod,
assign,test}.rs` in Bevy's own declaration order, plus the light systems that stayed in
`bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs`, the cluster buffers in `bevy_pbr/src/cluster.rs`, the render-world
visible-entity types in `bevy_pbr/src/components.rs`, and a small set of `PARENT:` rows for the
`render`/`camera`/`transform` entities those files consume.

Three rows in this section may combine mechanically-identical sibling entities (a whole flag-constant
family, a run of scalar fields whose Epix counterpart is one struct with one verdict, a group of
pure accessors). Every named entity of every audited Bevy file still appears in some row; where a
row covers more than one, the Entity cell names all of them.

**Headline finding.** Epix ports the *simulation* half of the 0.18 light split — the component
types, their defaults and constants, the cascade builder and the whole cluster-assignment
arithmetic — and almost none of the *render* half. `LightPlugin`, every render-world extraction and
preparation system (`extract_lights`, `prepare_lights`, `extract_clusters`, `prepare_clusters`,
`init_shadow_samplers`, the three specialisation systems, `queue_shadows`), both shadow-pass graph
nodes and the four render-world visible-entity types are absent, and no plugin registers *anything*
in `epix_engine/pbr` — so the light component types are not even registered as components with
their Bevy required-component relations. Three concrete defects sit inside the code that *is*
ported: cluster assignment never tests `RenderLayers` (assign.rs:541 has no counterpart), it never
writes `Clusters::near`/`far` (assign.rs:455-456), and it neither clears nor resizes
`Clusters::clusterable_objects` (assign.rs:465-477) — so `Clusters` stays empty and the next
`insert_object_into_cluster_row` indexes out of bounds.

| PBR-856 | def | `RenderMaterialInstance`, `RenderMaterialInstances` and the `DUMMY_MESH_MATERIAL` sentinel - the render world's record of which material each mesh uses | `bevy_pbr/src/material.rs:429,571-607` | `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/material.hpp` | ✅ | The records are untyped, as Bevy's are, so one map holds every mesh's material whatever type it is. `mesh_material` falls back to the sentinel rather than failing, which is what lets a mesh drawn by a custom pipeline still get a binding, and `current_change_tick` is carried for the sweep. Bevy's sentinel is typed `AssetId<StandardMaterial>` and converted where it is used; `StandardMaterial` is not ported, so it is untyped here and stands for "no material at all". `MaterialRegistry.MeshMaterialFallsBackToTheDummy` checks the fallback. |

| PBR-882 | system | `sweep_entities_needing_specialization<M>` - drops the bookkeeping of entities that lost their material | `bevy_pbr/src/material.rs:820-880` | `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/material.hpp` | ⚠️ | **Batch 128:** ported, registered after the extraction set so the tick it reads has already been recorded. An entity whose tick was **updated this frame** is kept rather than swept, which is what distinguishes a material replaced by one of another type - present in the removed list *and* re-added - from a material genuinely lost. **Two divergences recorded:** Bevy also clears the *prepass* and *shadow* pipeline caches here, through two optional resources that do not exist in the port (they belong to those features); and **the driving test is owed** - staging it needs a frame in which the removal event and an empty specialization queue coincide, which the batch-128 attempt did not get right, so the test asserts the extraction half only. The row says so rather than implying coverage. **Batch 129: the test question narrowed.** A second attempt did stage the tick half correctly - run a frame so the PostUpdate system fills the queue, extract, and the extraction records a tick for the visible mesh, which now asserts green. What still fails is the sweep itself: with the queue emptied by hand and the material removed in the same frame, so the removal is visible to the extraction and nothing re-records the entity, the sweep still **keeps** it. Since the keep-condition is `material_instances_tick == current_change_tick`, and the entity is no longer queued, the open question is now specific: whether `RemovedComponents<MeshMaterial3d<M>>` reaches an extract system at all in this port, or whether the tick comparison is reading different values than the staging assumes. That is a question to answer by reading, not a staging to guess at, so the test stays at the extraction half. **Batch 130: the first hypothesis eliminated by reading.** `Extract<T>` is generic - `SystemParam<Extract<T>> : SystemParam<T>` and its `init_state` builds the parameter against the `ExtractedWorld` resource, the main world - so **every** parameter inside `Extract` reads main-world state, `RemovedComponents<T>` included. Removal events do reach extract systems, so the sweep is not reading the wrong world. That leaves the second reading: the tick comparison itself. The next round on this should *measure* rather than stage - assert the recorded `material_instances_tick` against `RenderMaterialInstances::current_change_tick` at the moment the sweep runs - which distinguishes "the sweep never ran" from "it ran and its condition was true". **Batch 131: the measurement answered it, and found a real bug.** Printing the sweep's two inputs either side of a removal showed `recorded=2, registry=3` - the registry is bumped by `late_sweep` at the *end* of the run, so within the run the recorded tick and the current one are equal and the sweep keeps the entity. That is the code behaving as Bevy intends: an entity queued this frame keeps its bookkeeping. But the port was also logging `parameter validation error ... sweep entities needing material specialization`, so **the sweep had never run at all**: `MaterialPlugin` created `EntitySpecializationTicks` but not `SpecializedMaterialPipelineCache`, which the sweep takes as a parameter. The plugin now creates it and the validation error is gone - the same omission class as `EntitiesNeedingSpecialization`, found the same way. The test is still owed: with the sweep running, staging "lost its material" needs the entity to have settled a frame earlier *and* the removal to be in the same frame as the extraction, which the batch-131 attempts did not get to pass. **Batch 133: the test is delivered.** Batch 131's measurement made the staging possible: the sweep keeps an entity whose tick was recorded in the same run, so the entity settles a frame first - out of the specialization queue - and the removal then happens in the same frame as the extraction, because a frame in between is long enough for the removal event to be gone by the time the sweep reads it. `MaterialExtract` now spawns a second mesh, lets it settle, removes its material, extracts, and asserts the sweep cleared its bookkeeping. The row stays ⚠️ for the one divergence it still carries: Bevy also clears the prepass and shadow pipeline caches here, through two optional resources the port lacks. |

The 5 ❌ rows are the actionable findings, after the eighteen fixed so far
(PBR-707/708/713 in `cf484b87`, PBR-595 in `c43326c0`, PBR-604/605/606/609 in
`9badb75a`, PBR-576/682/798/840 in `636a72c6`, PBR-520/526/530 in

PBR-826 in `8a08e14a`). One is a diagnostic gap — PBR-796's two
remaining warnings, which need `prepare_lights` — and one is the unread
`NotShadowReceiver` (PBR-508). The other
three are whole-system halves whose pure functions already exist: `prepare_lights`' shadow textures
(PBR-777) and light views (PBR-778), and the `prepare_clusters` system half
(PBR-827), which needs `MeshPipeline` (`PBR-184`) for its binding type.

The 56 🚫 rows are dominated by one fact: **Epix has no render-world light half and no light
plugin.** `LightPlugin`, `ShadowFilteringMethod`, `SimulationLightSystems`, `add_clusters`,
`make_global_cluster_settings`, `init_global_clusterable_object_meta`, `init_shadow_samplers`,
`extract_lights`/`extract_ambient_light*`, `prepare_lights`, `queue_shadows`, `specialize_shadows`,
both shadow graph nodes and the three `Render*VisibleEntities` types are all absent, and nothing in
`epix_engine/pbr` registers a component or a resource. What *is* ported is ported well: the whole
cluster-assignment arithmetic, the cascade split and frustum construction, the GPU uniform layout
(with explicit tail padding where glm's alignment differs from Rust's `ShaderType`), and the
flag/bit contracts all match, which is why 264 rows are ✅.

The 29 ⚠️ rows partition as: enum-payload flattening (5: PBR-653/657/694/771/811), the PCSS
feature-gated light fields (3: PBR-567/585/599), explicit shader-type tail padding where glm's
alignment differs from Rust's `ShaderType` (3: PBR-745/746/750), Windows-macro and `_value`
renamings (3: PBR-663/786/810), `Color`-less linear colours (2: PBR-532/537), typed exceptions in
place of Bevy panics (2: PBR-551/676), the matrix-only `GlobalTransform` decomposition (2:
PBR-561/855), handle defaults (2: PBR-571/613), and one each for the probe-gather type shape
(PBR-635), the build-vs-system split of the directional cascade frusta (PBR-578), raw-set access to
`GlobalVisibleClusterableObjects` (PBR-686), the extra `default_gpu_lights()` factory (PBR-752), the
`PhaseItem` const/non-const overloads (PBR-790) and the `PARENT:` camera helper (PBR-854).

Two namespace facts came with it: `Cascades` and `CascadeShadowConfig` are `epix::pbr` types, while `CascadesFrusta` and `CascadesVisibleEntities` are `epix::camera` ones. **Verified with the two other kinds in the example: `assigned_objects` 60 to 120, global clusterable count 1 to 2.** |
| PBR-892 | def | The family: components that omit the required components Bevy puts on them | `bevy_ecs` `#[require(..)]` as used throughout `bevy_light`/`bevy_camera` | `none` - it is a class of omission, not one site | ❌ | **Batch 209: a family row, because this has now been sighted four times and is systematic rather than incidental.** Instances: `PRT-7` (`Camera3d` carries no `Projection`, so the mesh view key always read the nonstandard case); `PointLight` carrying no `Visibility` (`PBR-891`); and `GlobalClusterSettings` being read by a system that nothing ever inserted (`PBR-890`) - the same failure with a resource rather than a component. Each was found by running the code in an app rather than by reading it, and each was invisible to tests that drive schedules directly. **The pattern to audit:** for every ported component, compare Bevy's `#[require(..)]` list against this port's `register_required_components`, which is where the port expresses them (`camera.cpp:163` and `point_light.hpp:78` are the two positive examples). This row exists so that the next sighting is recognised as the fourth of a family rather than as a new surprise. **Batch 210: the audit this row asked for found two more, immediately.** `SpotLight` requires `#[require(Frustum, VisibleMeshEntities, Transform, Visibility, VisibilityClass)]` (`bevy_light/src/spot_light.rs:24`) and `DirectionalLight` requires `#[require(Cascades, CascadesFrusta, CascadeShadowConfig, CascadesVisibleEntities, Transform, Visibility, VisibilityClass)]`; this port registers requirements for `SpotLightTexture` but not `SpotLight`, and for `DirectionalLight` registers **nothing at all**. Both are therefore subject to exactly the bug `PBR-891` fixed for point lights - no `Visibility`, no `ViewVisibility`, never clustered, casting nothing - and both are unfixed only because the insert point inside each struct needs a read rather than a guess. Every named type exists in this port. **The audit method that produced this, worth repeating:** grep Bevy `#[require(` lines above the struct, grep the port for `register_required_components` in the matching header, and compare. **Batch 211: the light sweep is complete.** `SpotLight` and `DirectionalLight` are fixed on `PBR-893` and `PBR-894`, so every light component now registers what Bevy requires, and the example spawns one of each kind so that each is exercised - a per-kind requirement is only tested by its own kind, which is how the other two stayed hidden while `PointLight` was fixed. **A fifth instance was claimed and withdrawn.** `PRT-7` said `Camera3d` carries no `Projection`; it does - `Camera3d::register_required_components` registers one at `camera.hpp:433-435`, mirroring Bevy, and the port `Camera` hook lists exactly Bevy own set. The real defect is `PBR-895`, and it is in `pbr` rather than `camera`: the specialisation query tests the separate `PerspectiveProjection`/`OrthographicProjection` components where the requirement supplies `Projection`. **Batch 213: and that defect is fixed** - the query reads `Projection` and the arm switches on its variant, with the example workaround deleted so the fix is tested without it. **The lesson is this row own instruction, applied to itself:** check against the hook before recording a sighting, which is what the user did and I had not. The rest of the sweep is any other ported component with a Bevy `#[require(..)]` list. **Batch 221: the family has a header variant, and that time I was the author.** A hook or header that names types it does not declare fails the same way a component missing its requirements does - it compiles only where something else has already supplied the name. Two instances now: `material.hpp` called `app_register_asset` without the header that declares it (batch 192, hit by the first translation unit to include it directly), and `directional_light.hpp` named `Cascades`, `CascadeShadowConfig` and two companions in the required-components hook added in batch 211 without declaring any of them, which surfaced the moment `light_prepare.cpp` included it first (batch 221, forty errors). **The fix is the same in both: the header provides what it names.** Both were found by a new includer, which is the same way every component instance in this row was found - by using the code somewhere new. |
| PBR-890 | fn | `make_global_cluster_settings(world)` - reads the device and adapter to decide whether clustered forward has storage buffers and clustered decals, and builds the resource the assignment reads | `bevy_pbr/src/cluster.rs:38-53` | `none` | ✅ | **Batch 206: the reason clustering gathers nothing.** `assign_objects_to_clusters` opens with `if (!global_cluster_settings.has_value()) return;` (`light_systems.cpp:232`), and `GlobalClusterSettings` (`light_cluster.hpp:36`) is read in two places and **inserted nowhere** - no `init_resource` for it exists anywhere in the port. So the system returns before its first statement every frame, which is exactly what the cluster probe measured: `Clusters` present from `add_clusters` but still carrying the defaults it wrote, and a global clusterable count of zero. **The diagnosis is measured, not inferred:** the probe was committed first (batch 205) precisely so the fix is verified by it rather than by inspection. **Correcting batch 205 note:** it blamed a missing `ClusterableObjectType` requirement, which is wrong - Bevy has no such requirement, the type is a value the assignment constructs per object (`assign.rs:180`). **Fix owed:** port `make_global_cluster_settings`, which reads device and adapter capabilities, so this port passes those as parameters as it does elsewhere, and insert the result where Bevy inserts it. **Batch 207: fixed and verified.** `make_global_cluster_settings` is ported from `bevy_pbr/src/cluster.rs:38-53` with the two device and adapter capability facts as parameters, and the result is inserted from `PbrPlugin` - in the finish hook rather than build, and into the **main** app rather than the render world, which is where Bevy does it (`lib.rs:364-371`) and where `assign_objects_to_clusters` can see it. Verified by the cluster probe against the expectation stated when the fix was owed: `dimensions` went from the `(1,1,1)` default to `(17,9,24)`, `tile_size` from `(0,0)` to `(76,80)`, and `cluster_slots` from 0 to 3672. |

## Not audited

- **Shaders.** `mesh_view_types.wgsl`, `pbr.wgsl`, `shadows.wgsl`, `volumetric_fog.wgsl` and Epix's
  WGSL were not compared. Every flag/bit contract in this section is asserted only on the
  Rust/Epix side; the shader half of "these must match the bit flags in …" is unchecked.
- **Reflection and derive boilerplate.** `Reflect`, `#[reflect(...)]`, `Component`, `Resource`,
  `Deref`/`DerefMut` derives and their Epix equivalents are not rowed beyond the registration rows
  (PBR-502, PBR-687); Epix has no reflection layer to compare against.
- **`bevy_pbr` shader/pipeline internals consumed by `light.rs`.** `PrepassPipeline`,
  `PrepassPipelineSpecializer`, `ErasedMaterialPipelineKey`, `EntitiesNeedingSpecialization`,
  `EntitySpecializationTicks`, `RenderMaterialInstances`, `RenderMeshInstances`,
  `RenderLightmaps`, `ShadowsDrawFunction`, `MeshAllocator::mesh_slabs` and `SlabId` are referenced
  only as the reasons rows PBR-780..PBR-785 are 🚫; none of them was audited against its Epix
  counterpart. `RenderMeshInstances` is covered by the `render/mesh.rs` section.
- **`bevy_pbr/src/render/mesh.rs`.** The `Shadow` phase's plugin registration, `DrawFunctions`,
  `SetMeshBindGroup`/`DrawMesh` and the binned-phase plumbing belong to the `PBR-100`..`PBR-278`
  section (PBR-850 marks the boundary).
- **`bevy_pbr/src/render/light.rs` bodies of the systems recorded as 🚫.** For those rows the
  Bevy body was read and the *capability* it needs is named, but no Epix-side line can exist to
  diff against; the rows are therefore evidence of absence, not line-level comparison.
- **`bevy_pbr/src/light_probe/mod.rs` beyond the gather defs.** Only lines 300-419 and 550-651
  were read, for PBR-627..PBR-640; the rest of that file (bind groups, texture binding arrays,
  `upload_light_probes`' body) was not audited.
- **Epix tests.** `epix_engine/pbr/tests/header/cluster_tests.cpp` (4927 lines) was
  grep-scanned, not read in full. It is cited only as evidence that a behaviour is exercised — in
  particular `assign_objects_to_clusters` at `:3508` pre-resizes `clusterable_objects`, which is
  what proves PBR-708's missing resize is real rather than a call-order artefact.
- **The `DistanceFog` half of `epix_engine/pbr/src/fog.cpp`.** `prepare_fog` is Bevy's
  distance-fog system (`bevy_pbr/src/fog.rs`), a different module from
  `bevy_light/src/volumetric.rs`; PBR-650 records the boundary.
- **`epix_engine/pbr/tests/**` and `epix_engine/pbr/include/epix/pbr/{mesh_pipeline,
  mesh_pipeline_key,mesh_instance,mesh_uniform,material_bindings}.hpp`** — out of this section's
  scope; they belong to `PBR-100`..`PBR-278`.

Camera module — `bevy_camera`

Scope: Bevy's `bevy_camera` crate, which this port spreads across `camera/` (the `Camera`
component, its components, projections, visibility, clear colour) and the parts of the
render world it feeds. **Brought into the audit in batch 225 at the user's direction**, so
the section opens with what earlier batches already found rather than an empty sheet: the
required-components family (`PBR-892`) has twice had camera-side instances, and the rows
below are those, recorded here instead of as `PARENT: camera` notes on other modules'
rows.

Counts: ✅ 45 · ❌ 3 · ⚠️ 20 · 🚫 11 · ⛔ 1 (80 rows, `CAM-1`..`CAM-81`).

**Checked and matching, so deliberately without a row.** `Camera2d` and `Camera3d`'s
required components (`camera.hpp:433-451`) match Bevy's `#[require(..)]` lists item for
item: both require `Camera` and a `Projection`, and `Camera2d`'s `Frustum` is computed from
the 2D orthographic projection rather than defaulted, exactly as Bevy writes it
(`components.rs:11-15`). Recorded because this is the area the required-components family
(`PBR-892`) has tripped over three times, and because a withdrawn row (`PRT-7`) once claimed
the opposite about `Camera3d`.

| ID | kind | What Bevy has | Bevy reference | Epix | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CAM-1 | const | `CUBE_MAP_FACES` — the six `CubeMapFace` values (`target`, `up`) the cube-face rotations are derived from, `[+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z]`, with the left-handed convention that maps the `+Z` face to `-Z` | `bevy_camera/src/primitives.rs:439-470` | `epix_engine/camera/include/epix/camera/visibility.hpp:547-554` | ✅ | Fixed: renamed to `CUBE_MAP_FACES`, Bevy spelling, at the definition (`visibility.hpp`) and both call sites (`pbr/src/shadow_phase.cpp`). The data was always present and correct under the other name - the audit had once searched Bevy name and reported the array absent, which is why the spelling is not cosmetic. Verified with the batch. |
| CAM-2 | plugin | `VisibilityPlugin` registers `Visibility` and `VisibilityClass` for `Mesh3d`, plus a `Mesh3d` on_add hook that appends the Mesh3d class | bevy_camera/src/visibility/mod.rs:397-400,430-435 | `epix_engine/camera/src/camera.cpp:450-452` (Mesh2d only); `epix_engine/mesh/include/epix/mesh/components.hpp:39-55` | ✅ | Fixed in `b9e28111`: `VisibilityPlugin` registers `Visibility` and `VisibilityClass` for `Mesh3d`, as Bevy does. This row was left diverging after the fix, which is the tracker drift the audit already warns about - an open row must be re-verified against the current code before it is acted on. Verified then and unchanged since: build clean, CTest passing, and the 2D baseline capture on its hash. **Note:** the registration uses the `Mesh3d` type defined in `mesh/components.hpp`, whose own required-components hook also registers `Visibility` for the pair - both are needed, because `VisibilityPlugin` covers entities spawned without `MeshPlugin`. |
| CAM-3 | system | `check_visibility` takes `visible_entity_ranges: Option<Res<VisibleEntityRanges>>` | bevy_camera/src/visibility/mod.rs:609,649-655 | `epix_engine/camera/include/epix/camera/visibility.hpp:692`, `camera/src/camera.cpp:369` | ✅ | **Verified by direct read.** Epix takes a required `ResMut<VisibleEntityRanges>`, which only `VisibilityRangePlugin` initialises (`camera.cpp:409`), so with `VisibilityPlugin` attached alone the parameter fails validation, the executor logs and skips the system, and no `ViewVisibility`/`VisibleEntities` is produced at all - where Bevy runs it and merely skips range culling. The port already uses the optional idiom elsewhere (`std::optional<ecs::Res<VisibleEntityRanges>>`, `pbr/include/epix/pbr/light_systems.hpp:210`), so this is an omission rather than a limitation. **Fixed in `2ed32a3a`.** The parameter is now `std::optional<ecs::Res<VisibleEntityRanges>>` in both the declaration and the definition, with its single use guarded, so `VisibilityPlugin` alone no longer leaves the system skipped. Verified: build zero errors, CTest 112/112, and the 2D baseline capture hashes `DBABB1D0` unchanged. **This is the other half of `CAM-2`:** that fix made a `Mesh3d` eligible to be visible, this one makes `check_visibility` run to mark it. |

## Not yet audited inside this module

Nothing: `bevy_camera` is now covered file by file. The nine files and the rows that
cover them are `camera.rs` (`CAM-4`..`CAM-11`), `clear_color.rs` (`CAM-47`..`CAM-49`),
`components.rs` (`CAM-12`, `CAM-13`), `lib.rs` (`CAM-53`..`CAM-56`), `primitives.rs`
(`CAM-1`, `CAM-36`..`CAM-46`), `projection.rs` (`CAM-14`..`CAM-17`), `visibility/mod.rs`
(`CAM-2`, `CAM-3`, `CAM-18`..`CAM-26`), `visibility/range.rs` (`CAM-58`..`CAM-81`) and
`visibility/render_layers.rs` (`CAM-27`..`CAM-35`), plus the camera-owned `bevy_render`
items `texture/manual_texture_view.rs` (`CAM-50`..`CAM-52`) and `view/mod.rs` (`CAM-49`).

The only camera-adjacent work left is not this crate's: `bevy_render/src/view/visibility/range.rs`
(`RenderVisibilityRanges`, `VISIBILITY_RANGES_STORAGE_BUFFER_COUNT`, `VISIBILITY_RANGE_UNIFORM_BUFFER_SIZE`,
`extract_visibility_ranges`, `write_render_visibility_ranges`) mirrors Bevy's *render* copy of the
range types, and is tracked by the render/core_graph sections rather than here. `CAM-47` cannot be
closed inside the camera module: it waits on the `color` port.

# COL-1..COL-58 — `bevy_color/src/color.rs` + `bevy_color/src/lib.rs`, entity by entity

Scope: the whole of `crates/bevy_color/src/color.rs` (912 lines) and the whole of
`crates/bevy_color/src/lib.rs` (279 lines): the `Color` enum, its constructors and constants, its
`Default`/`Alpha`/cross-space `From` impls, the operation-trait impls written in `color.rs`
(`Luminance`, `Hue`, `Saturation`, `Mix`, `EuclideanDistance`, `TryStableInterpolate`), the
`ChosenColorSpace` alias, the crate's module list, the `prelude`, the crate-root re-exports, the
`StandardColor` marker trait and the `impl_componentwise_vector_space` macro with the operator and
`bevy_math` impls it generates. One extra row (`COL-58`, `ColorToComponents`) is included only
because the brief names it; that trait is declared in `crates/bevy_color/src/color_ops.rs:127-145`,
not in `color.rs`, and its line numbers are cited from that file.

**Two brief items have no Bevy counterpart, so they get no row.** (a) `ColorFromComponents` does not
exist in Bevy 0.18: a content search over the whole pinned tree
(`tmp/bevy-0.18.0`, all `*.rs`, `*.toml`, `*.md`, `*.wgsl`) returns zero matches; 0.18 folded the
old conversion entry points into `ColorToComponents` as its `from_*` methods (`color_ops.rs:137-144`).
(b) There is no color plugin: the same whole-tree search for `ColorPlugin` returns zero matches, and
`bevy_color` has no `plugin.rs`, no `impl Plugin` and no plugin type. The port registers no color
plugin either.

Bevy source pinned at `tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/`. Bevy files read in full: `bevy_color/src/color.rs`,
`bevy_color/src/lib.rs`; read in part: `bevy_color/src/color_ops.rs:100-179`,
`bevy_camera/src/clear_color.rs:1-62` (reference only, for the `ClearColor` default).

The port was searched **by content**, not by name, over all of `epix_engine/**` (`*.hpp`, `*.cpp`,
`*.cc`, `*.h`, embedded Slang in `.cpp`), and over `tests/**` and `examples/**` read-only:
`Color`, `struct/class/enum class/using Color =`, `Srgba`, `Srgba8`, `LinearRgba`, `Hsla`, `Hsva`,
`Hwba`, `Laba`, `Lcha`, `Oklaba`, `Oklcha`, `Xyza` (case-insensitive), `to_linear`, `to_srgba`,
`gamma_function`, `srgb_to_linear`, `linear_to_srgb`, `is_srgb`, `srgb_texture_format`,
`srgb_view_formats`, `with_alpha`, `set_alpha`, `interpolate_stable`, `TryStableInterpolate`,
`VectorSpace`, `StandardColor`, `MismatchedUnits`, `EuclideanDistance`, `distance_squared`, `Mix`,
`glm::mix`, `prelude`, `ColorSpace`, `hsl`, `hsv`, `hwb`, `lab`, `lch`, `oklab`, `oklch`, `xyz`,
`to_vec4`, `to_vec3`, `from_vec4`, `to_f32_array`, `to_u8_array`, `from_u8_array`, `ColorPlugin`,
`rotate_hue`, `from_rgb`, `BLACK`, `black`. The explicitly named hiding places were checked:
`epix_engine/camera/include/epix/camera/clear_color.hpp` and the image module's sRGB texture-format
helpers (`epix_engine/image/src/image.cpp`, `epix_engine/image/src/image_texture_conversion.cpp`,
`epix_engine/image/include/epix/image/image.hpp`).

Findings that frame every row: there is **no color module and no color type** anywhere in the port.
No `namespace epix::color`, no `epix/color` include, no `Color` alias, and no declaration of any of
Bevy's color-space type names. The only occurrences of those names in the port are **comments**
(`image.cpp:910,915,920`; `sprite_render/src/tilemap_chunk_material.cpp:98,103,105`;
`render/core_graph/src/core3d.cpp:1092`; `pbr/include/epix/pbr/light_meta.hpp:174`;
`pbr/include/epix/pbr/fog.hpp:62`; `camera/include/epix/camera/clear_color.hpp:12`) — a grep hit is
not a declaration. Every color in the port is an untyped linear `glm::vec4`
(`ClearColor : public glm::vec4`, `clear_color.hpp:11`), so linear-space capability is present as
plain data while every sRGB/HSL/HSV/HWB/Lab/Lch/Oklab/Oklch/XYZ type, transfer entry point and
operation entry point is not.

Status convention used here (recorded because the port has no `Color` type at all): 🚫 = no
implementation of the item's semantics found anywhere in the port; ❌ = the item's semantics exist
somewhere in the port but under a different name, file or type shape (the note says where); ⚠️/✅
were not awarded to any row, because no row is an actual counterpart of a `bevy_color` item.

| COL-1 | enum | `Color` — 10-variant enum over `Srgba`/`LinearRgba`/`Hsla`/`Hsva`/`Hwba`/`Laba`/`Lcha`/`Oklaba`/`Oklcha`/`Xyza`, with `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq`, derived `From`, and feature-gated `Reflect`/`Serialize` | bevy_color/src/color.rs:45-77 | none | 🚫 | No color type of any kind in the port: no `enum class Color`, no `struct Color`, no `using Color = ...` (content searches return 0 hits). No storage form exists for a color that is not linear RGBA, so the "store a color that cannot be generic over its space" purpose has no counterpart. |

# Color audit — part 2: `srgba.rs` and `linear_rgba.rs`

**Bevy files audited (read in full):**
- `tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/bevy_color/src/srgba.rs` (521 lines)
- `tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/bevy_color/src/linear_rgba.rs` (478 lines)

Supporting Bevy reads (only where a port mapping needed the referenced semantics): `crates/bevy_color/src/lib.rs:170-279` (the body of `impl_componentwise_vector_space!`), `crates/bevy_color/src/xyza.rs:205-244` (`From<LinearRgba> for Xyza`).

**Port searches run (by content, over all of `epix_engine/`, not by name):**
- sRGB transfer constants/formulas: `0.04045`, `12.92`, `0.0031308`, `1.055`, `powf`/`pow(..., 2.4f)`, `1.0f / 2.4f`
- luminance / XYZ: `0.2126`, `0.7152`, `0.0722`, `0.2126f`, `0.2126729`, `0.7151522`, `0.0721750`, `0.4124564`, `0.3575761`, `3.2404542`, `1.5371385`, `luminance`, `Xyza`, `xyz`
- type names and spellings: `Srgba`, `LinearRgba`, `Srgb`, `srgb`, `LinearRgb`, `linear_rgb`, `SrgbColor`, `SrgbaColor`, `LinearColor`, `Color::`, `to_srgba`, `to_linear`
- methods/impls: `gamma_function`, `gamma_function_inverse`, `to_u8_array`, `to_u8_array_no_alpha`, `from_u8_array`, `with_alpha`, `set_alpha`, `with_red`, `with_green`, `with_blue`, `with_luminance`, `adjust_lightness`, `mix_assign`, `distance_squared`, `EuclideanDistance`, `StandardColor`, `ColorToComponents`, `ColorToPacked`, `impl_componentwise`, `Mix`, `Gray`, `to_vec4`, `to_f32_array`
- hex and u8 constructors: `from_str_radix`, `hex(`, `to_hex`, `HexColorError`, `srgb_u8`, `from_chars`, `0123456789abcdef`, `, 16)`
- named color constants: `WHITE`, `BLACK`, `NONE`, `RED`, `GREEN`, `BLUE`, `constexpr glm::vec4`, `quiet_NaN`
- GPU/packing integration: `wgpu::Color`, `ShaderTypeInfo`, `ShaderTypeInfo<glm::vec`, `glm::mix(`, `from_le_bytes`, `<< 24`
- texture-byte paths named in the brief: `image.cpp` (`srgb_to_linear`/`linear_to_srgb`/`luminance`/`/ 255.0f`), `camera/include/epix/camera/clear_color.hpp`, `sprite_render/src/tilemap_chunk_material.cpp`
- full directory enumeration of `epix_engine/` (20 top-level modules; **no** color module exists — colors are raw `glm::vec4` throughout, which the port states itself at `sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/color_material.hpp:34-35`, `pbr/include/epix/pbr/ambient_light.hpp:16-17` and `image/include/epix/image/image.hpp:1183-1186`)

**Status convention used here** (the port has no sRGB/linear color *type*, so several Bevy methods survive only as free functions or inline expressions on `glm::vec4`):
- 🚫 = no value, constant, helper or expression in the port performs this operation.
- ❌ = the port performs it, but the computed behaviour differs.
- ⚠️ = the port performs the same component-wise operation, but through a different spelling/structure (no color type), which the port documents.
- ✅ = exact match including structure.

**Scope flag for another auditor (not counted as a row here):** `epix_engine/image/src/image.cpp:881-885` defines `to_u8` as *truncation* (`static_cast<uint8_t>(value * 255)`), while `ColorToPacked::to_u8_array` rounds. Whether that function corresponds to a rounding Bevy item is an `image.rs` question and is out of this section's scope.

# Colour part 3 — the remaining colour spaces

Scope: the six remaining `bevy_color` colour-space files, read in full at
`tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/bevy_color/src/`: `hsla.rs` (455 lines), `hsva.rs` (335), `hwba.rs` (343),
`laba.rs` (427), `lcha.rs` (400), `xyza.rs` (285). Rows follow Bevy's declaration order inside each
file; the two directions of one conversion are one `impl` row. `Oklaba`/`Oklcha` themselves belong to
another agent's range — only the `Oklaba` conversions that `laba.rs` itself declares appear here.
None of the six files declares a free function, so no `fn` row appears: every `fn` in them is a
trait-impl member or sits inside `mod tests`, and both are covered per file. The shared helpers they
call (`color_ops::lerp_hue`, `impl_componentwise_vector_space!`) live in `bevy_color` files outside
this scope.

No `epix_engine` file under any of these was modified; this section is read-only evidence.

Port searched **by content, not by name** (all of `epix_engine/`, plus `tests/`, `examples/` and
`libs/` repo-wide):

- `(?i)whiteness|blackness|chroma|lightness|saturation` → 24 hits, all `ColorGrading`/tonemapping
  `saturation` fields and shader locals; no colour-space content.
- `0.4124564|0.95047|1.08883|D65|CIE_EPSILON|24389` → 1 hit, a doc comment in
  `render/render/include/epix/render/color_grading.hpp:122`.
- `(?i)\bhue\b|hsla|hsva|hwba|laba|lcha|xyza|oklaba|oklcha` → 21 hits, all the colour-grading `hue`
  (radians) field, `.xyz` swizzles and unrelated identifiers.
- `lerp_hue|sequential_dispersed|2654435769|golden_ratio|GOLDEN` → 0 hits.
- `(?i)\bhsl\b|\bhsv\b|\bhwb\b|\blch\b|\blab\b|\bxyz\b|oklab|oklch` → 54 hits: the light-cluster
  `Kind::XYZ` variants and `.xyz` vector swizzles only.
- `rgb_to_hsv|hsv_to_rgb|rgb_to_hsl|hsl_to_rgb` → 6 hits, all inside the tonemapping Slang source.
- `(?i)with_luminance|darker|lighter|\bMix\b|StandardColor|\bGray\b|ColorToComponents|to_f32_array|componentwise`
  → 8 hits, none a colour-space trait.
- `3.2404542|1.5371385|0.2126729|0.7151522|0.0721750|216.0|24389.0|116.0|with_alpha|set_alpha`
  → 1 hit, `image/src/image.cpp:911` (see CSP-203).
- Repo-wide `(?i)\bHsla\b|\bHsva\b|\bHwba\b|\bLaba\b|\bLcha\b|\bXyza\b` and
  `hsl_to|hwb_to|lab_to|lch_to|xyz_to` → comments (`image.cpp:910`), a tracker row
  (`documentation/bevy-0.18-module-mismatch-tracker.md:4161,4218`), third-party ImGui `"HSVA"` colour
  picker labels (`libs/imgui`, `libs/tracy`), and `slab_to_reallocate` false positives. `tests/` and
  `examples/` contain nothing.

Result: the port has **no colour-space value types at all**; every colour is a `glm::vec4` and the
headers state the reason (`sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/tilemap_chunk.hpp:53` "Bevy stores
a tagged `Color`; Epix has no `bevy_color`"; `pbr/include/epix/pbr/point_light.hpp:19`;
`image/include/epix/image/image.hpp:1185` "Epix has no `Color` value type"). One content-only match is
recorded as a row rather than reported absent: the Y row of Bevy's linear-sRGB→XYZ matrix (CSP-203,
❌). A second content-only candidate is deliberately **not** a row: the HSV round trip that exists
**only inside the tonemapping Slang shader** (`tonemapping.cpp:79-97`) is faithful to
`bevy_render/src/color_operations.wgsl` — a different Bevy file, with hue in **radians** — and so is
not a port of `hsva.rs`.

Also checked because the task named them: `camera/include/epix/camera/clear_color.hpp` (read in full,
51 lines) — its default is Bevy's `Color::srgb_u8(43, 44, 47)` expressed directly as a linear
`glm::vec4`; no HSL/HSV/HWB/LAB/LCH/XYZ content. `image/src/image.cpp:881-1002` — the sRGB
texture-format helpers are `Srgba::gamma_function` / `gamma_function_inverse` and
`Xyza::from(LinearRgba).y` ports only.

# Colour part 4 — Oklab and Oklch

Scope: the two Oklab-family `bevy_color` colour-space files, read in full at
`tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/bevy_color/src/`: `oklaba.rs` (400 lines) and `oklcha.rs` (439 lines).
Rows follow Bevy's declaration order inside each file; the two directions of one conversion are one
`impl` row (they are adjacent 2-line-body impls in both files). `Oklaba`/`Oklcha` live in these two
files only; the derived conversions that *other* files declare (`From<Oklaba> for Laba` at
`laba.rs:353-363`, the `Color::Oklaba`/`Color::Oklcha` enum arms in `color.rs`) are attributed to
their declaring file and belong to the sibling sections.

No file under `epix_engine/`, `tests/` or `examples/` was modified; this section is read-only
evidence.

**Row-id note:** the five `color-part*.md` sections were authored in parallel, so their `COL` id
ranges overlapped. Each part therefore carries its own tracker prefix — `COL` for part 1 (`color.rs`,
`lib.rs`), `CSL` for part 2 (`srgba.rs`, `linear_rgba.rs`), `CSP` for part 3 (the remaining colour
spaces), `COK` for part 4 (this file: `oklaba.rs`, `oklcha.rs`) and `COP` for part 5 (operations,
gradients, ranges, interpolation) — so the ids are unique in the merged tracker without renumbering
the evidence.

**Gamut handling — checked explicitly, because the brief names it.** Bevy 0.18's `bevy_color` has
**no** `gamut` module: `lib.rs:99-120` declares `color`, `color_difference`, `color_gradient`,
`color_ops`, `color_range`, `hsla`, `hsva`, `hwba`, `interpolate`, `laba`, `lcha`, `linear_rgba`,
`oklaba`, `oklcha`, `palettes`, `srgba`, `test_colors`, `testing`, `xyza` and nothing else. A
crate-wide search for `gamut` finds only prose (`color_ops.rs:11,17,25`) and a `clamp` call in
`lcha.rs:293` (which is `Lcha`'s own conversion, not Oklab's). So for these two spaces the entire
gamut behaviour is the `Luminance::darker`/`lighter` clamp to `[0, 1]` recorded in COK-134 and
COK-159; both `From` conversions are unclamped, and `Oklcha`'s `From<Oklaba>` at `oklcha.rs:257-273`
does **not** clamp chroma the way `From<Laba> for Lcha` (`lcha.rs:272-298`) clamps it to `1.5`. No
separate gamut row is invented, because no such Bevy item exists to port.

Port searched **by content, not by name** (all of `epix_engine/`, plus repo-wide `tests/`,
`examples/`, `libs/`, `assets/`, and the `documentation/` trackers):

- `oklab|oklch|Oklab|Oklch` over every file of `epix_engine/` → **0 hits**; repo-wide over
  `*.{hpp,cpp,h,c,md,json,cmake,txt,wgsl}` → **0 hits**. Even the name is never mentioned in a
  comment, unlike `LinearRgba`/`Srgba`/`Xyza`, which are named in comments at
  `pbr/include/epix/pbr/light_meta.hpp:174` and `image/src/image.cpp:910`.
- The Oklab matrix coefficients, searched individually: `0.41222146|0.21045426|1.9779985|
  0.39633778|0.105561346|4.0767417|0.2119035|0.08830246` → **0 hits**. The forward and inverse
  Oklab transforms therefore exist nowhere in the port under any spelling.
- `lightness|chroma|with_hue|set_hue|with_luminance|distance_squared|EuclideanDistance|
  ColorToComponents|StandardColor` → 11 hits, **all** the local variable `distance_squared` in
  `mesh/src/primitives.cpp:216,217,218,477,478,479,484,487,687,688,693`. `lightness`, `chroma`,
  `with_hue`, `with_luminance`, `EuclideanDistance`, `ColorToComponents` and `StandardColor` are
  **0 hits**.
- `sequential_dispersed|golden.ratio|2654435769|quasi.random|dispersed` → **0 hits**.
- `cbrt|hypot(|atan2|sin_cos|to_degrees|to_radians|lerp_hue` → 6 hits, all unrelated `std::atan2`
  (pixelbody body rotation, mesh azimuth/cone angle, fallingsand gravity angle,
  `render/render/src/maths.cpp:148`). No `cbrt`, no `hypot`, no `sin_cos`, no degree/radian
  conversion, no `lerp_hue`.
- `BLACK|WHITE|to_f32_array|from_f32_array|with_alpha|set_alpha|fn mix|mix_assign|
  is_fully_transparent` → 5 hits, all comments or shader-def strings (`WHITE_BALANCE` at
  `render/core_graph/src/tonemapping.cpp:256,533`, `Some(BLACK)` comments at
  `core_graph/src/core3d.cpp:905,1092`, `Color::WHITE` comment at
  `sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/wireframe2d.hpp:34`).
- `componentwise|VectorSpace|perceptual|Luminance|luminance` → 40 hits: `perceptual_roughness*`
  shader fields, the `Tonemapping::ReinhardLuminance` enum case, the Slang `tonemapping_luminance`
  helper, `illuminance` in lux, and the single colour-adjacent helper
  `image/src/image.cpp:909-912`. No vector-space trait and no colour-space `Luminance`.
- `gamma_function|linear_to_srgb|srgb_to_linear|to_u8_array|to_srgba` → the port's **only**
  colour-space code: `image/src/image.cpp:914-922` (`Srgba::gamma_function` and
  `gamma_function_inverse`, commented as such) and
  `sprite_render/src/tilemap_chunk_material.cpp:98-108` (the same transfer plus the `to_u8_array`
  rounding). Both are `Srgba`/`Color`-side helpers that route *through* a colour space; neither
  contains Oklab.
- `(?i)srgb` → 62 hits, every one a wgpu texture format or loader flag
  (`srgb_texture_format` at `image/src/image.cpp:612`, `srgb_view_formats` at
  `image/src/image.cpp:1463`, `TextureFormat::eRGBA8UnormSrgb`, `BGRA8UnormSrgb`, `R8UnormSrgb`,
  `Rg8UnormSrgb`, `Image::is_srgb`). None is a colour-space conversion.
- File discovery: glob `**/*color*` → only `camera/clear_color.hpp`,
  `render/render/include/epix/render/color_grading.hpp`, `sprite_render/.../color_material.{hpp,cpp}`;
  glob `**/*colour*` → **0 files**. `epix_engine/` has no `color`/`colour` module directory at all
  (its 22 top-level directories are `app`, `assets`, `camera`, `common`, `ecs`, `experimental`,
  `extension`, `image`, `input`, `mesh`, `pbr`, `render`, `shader`, `sprite`, `sprite_render`,
  `task`, `text`, `time`, `transform`, `utils`, `window`).

Checked because the brief names them:

- `camera/include/epix/camera/clear_color.hpp` (read in full, 51 lines) — `ClearColor : glm::vec4`
  whose default is `(0.02415763, 0.02518686, 0.02842604, 1.0)`, documented at line 12-13 as Bevy's
  `Color::srgb_u8(43, 44, 47)` written directly in linear space. No Oklab/Oklch content; the
  conversion Bevy performs through a colour space is skipped, not ported.
- `image/`'s sRGB texture-format helpers: `srgb_texture_format` (`image.cpp:612`) maps
  `Rgba8Unorm↔Rgba8UnormSrgb`-style pairs and `srgb_view_formats` (`image.cpp:1463`) returns the
  sRGB view-format set; the gamma helpers at `image.cpp:914-922` are `Srgba`'s. No Oklab content in
  either.
- The `documentation/` trackers state the reason repeatedly — "Epix has no `Color` type
  anywhere in the repo" / "no `bevy_color`" / "Epix has no colour crate, so the colour is a linear
  `glm::vec4`" (`pbr/include/epix/pbr/ambient_light.hpp:16`, `point_light.hpp:19`, `spot_light.hpp:21`,
  `sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/tilemap_chunk.hpp:53`, `wireframe2d.hpp:28`).

Result: the port has **no Oklab and no Oklch value type, conversion, constant or trait impl** — 0
content hits for every distinguishing coefficient, channel name and helper of both files — and it has
no colour-space value types generally, so all 52 rows below are absent. The single near-miss worth
recording rather than reporting absent is the port's inline use of *other* colour spaces' maths
(`Srgba`'s gamma pair and `Xyza`'s Y row) inside `image.cpp`; those are rows of the sibling sections,
not of `oklaba.rs`/`oklcha.rs`.

# Colour part 5 — operations, differences, gradients, ranges, interpolation

Scope: the five `bevy_color` files assigned to me, read in full at
`tmp/bevy-0.18.0/crates/bevy_color/src/`: `color_ops.rs` (225 lines),
`color_difference.rs` (15), `color_gradient.rs` (111), `color_range.rs` (46) and
`interpolate.rs` (37). Rows follow Bevy's declaration order per file. Test modules are not rowed;
where a file's only content is a test module (`interpolate.rs`) that fact is recorded on the module row.
`Oklaba`/`Xyza`/`Srgba` themselves are other agents' ranges; only the trait declarations and
trait-level defaults that these five files own appear here.

No file under `epix_engine/`, `tests/` or `examples/` was modified; this section is read-only evidence.

Port searched **by content, not by name** across all of `epix_engine/**/*.{hpp,cpp,h}` (479 files),
plus `tests/`, `examples/`, `documentation/` and `libs/` repo-wide:

- `luminance|with_luminance` → 29 hits: the CIE-Y free function `luminance(glm::vec4)`
  (`image/src/image.cpp:909`, used only by the luma texture-format packer at `:1009-1022`),
  `tonemapping_luminance` in the tonemapping Slang source, and light `illuminance` prose. No trait.
- `darker|lighter` → prose only (`render/render/include/epix/render/color_grading.hpp:56,60`,
  `pbr/include/epix/pbr/volumetric.hpp:64`).
- `mix_assign` → 0 hits. `\bmix\(` → 3 hits, all `glm::mix` on `glm::vec4` colours in
  `extension/fallingsand/src/systems.cpp:42,88,90`. `lerp|Lerp` → 28 hits, all hexasphere slerp,
  `std::lerp` on angles, and Slang `lerp`.
- `Gray|\bgray\(|\bBLACK\b|\bWHITE\b` → no colour constant or constructor; `BLACK`/`WHITE` appear only
  in comments (`sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/wireframe2d.hpp:34`,
  `render/core_graph/src/core3d.cpp:905,1092`).
- `with_alpha|set_alpha|\.alpha\(\)|is_fully_transparent|is_fully_opaque` → 0 hits.
  `is_opaque` → pipeline pass state (`pbr/include/epix/pbr/mesh_pipeline.hpp:106`).
- `with_hue|rotate_hue|set_hue|\bhue\b` → colour-grading uniforms in radians
  (`color_grading.hpp:25`) and the tonemapping shader's inline `hsv_to_rgb`/`rgb_to_hsv`
  (`render/core_graph/src/tonemapping.cpp:80-91,253`).
- `with_saturation|set_saturation|saturat` → grading uniforms (`color_grading.hpp:38`) and the AgX
  shader helper `saturation_` (`tonemapping.cpp:167-169`).
- `to_f32_array|from_f32_array|to_vec3|from_vec3|from_vec4|to_u8_array|from_u8_array` → `to_vec4` only
  (`camera/include/epix/camera/clear_color.hpp:17`, called at `render/render/src/view.cpp:241,243` and
  `render/core_graph/src/upscaling.cpp:45,51,54`); `to_vec3` is a mesh vertex helper
  (`mesh/src/mesh.cpp:601`). The other eight names: 0 hits.
- `ColorToPacked|ColorToComponents|color_component_to_u8|round.*255` → the ad-hoc per-channel packer
  `color_component_to_u8` (`sprite_render/src/tilemap_chunk_material.cpp:99-101`) plus `linear_to_srgb`
  (`:106`) used by `PackedTileData`'s ctor (`:117-121`).
- `EuclideanDistance|distance_squared|\bdistance\(` → local mesh-primitive variables only
  (`mesh/src/primitives.cpp:216,477,687`, `mesh/src/mesh.cpp`); `libs/` hits are gmock
  `EuclideanDistance`/`DistanceFrom` matchers and SDL3 `SDL_ColorRange`. `tests/` and `examples/`: 0 hits.
- `ColorCurve|ColorRange|EvenCore|\bCurve\b|\bInterval\b|sample_clamped|sample_unchecked` →
  `pbr/include/epix/pbr/scattering_medium.hpp:23-26,39-42` explicitly records that the port has no
  curve type; `SDL_ColorRange` (a pixel-range enum) and unrelated "gradient" prose
  (`volumetric.hpp:35`, `ssr.hpp:40`) are the remaining hits.
- `StableInterpolate|interpolate_stable` → 0 hits repo-wide.

Result: the port has **no colour module and no colour value type at all** — every colour is a linear
`glm::vec4`, stated by the port itself (`sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/color_material.hpp:34-35`,
`pbr/include/epix/pbr/ambient_light.hpp:16`, `pbr/include/epix/pbr/point_light.hpp:19`,
`sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/tilemap_chunk.hpp:53-54`,
`sprite_render/include/epix/sprite_render/wireframe2d.hpp:28`) and by the repo tracker
(`documentation/bevy-0.18-module-mismatch-tracker.md:7947`, CAM-47: "no `Color` type anywhere in the
repo"). So every trait below is absent in the strict sense. Convention used in the status column:
**🚫** = no counterpart of any kind found by content; **❌** = a same-purpose stand-in exists under a
different spelling or shape, named in the note. Notes cite only lines read with the read tool.

## Not yet audited

The eight modules are only partly covered: the sections above audit specific Bevy files. Still open, so the next round knows where to start —

- **`mesh` (`MSH-`, `PRT-`)** — the `mesh.rs` support files with no section yet: `bevy_mesh/src/vertex.rs` (`VertexAttributeValues` internals, `VertexBufferLayout`, `MeshVertexBufferLayout`, `MeshVertexBufferLayouts`, `MissingVertexAttributeError` bodies), `index.rs`, `components.rs`, `skinning.rs`, `morph.rs`, `lib.rs` (the `MeshPlugin` entity), `conversions.rs`, `mikktspace.rs` — against `epix_engine/mesh/include/epix/mesh/{vertex_attribute_values.hpp,vertex_buffer_layout.hpp,components.hpp}`. The mesh primitive builders are also unaudited: `bevy_mesh/src/primitives/**` against `epix_engine/mesh/include/epix/mesh/primitives.hpp` and `epix_engine/mesh/src/primitives.cpp` (`Triangle3d::mesh()`, `Triangle3dMeshBuilder`, `Measured2d`/`Measured3d`, `Inset`), plus the `bevy_math` primitive shapes they mirror (`bevy_math/src/primitives/**`; `Aabb3d` lives in `bevy_math::bounding`, and `Triangle3d` — whose MSH-218 row is already open — has its home there too). `mesh/src/mesh_factory.cpp` is Epix-only and has no Bevy file to diff.
- **`image` (`IMG-`)** — `image.rs` and the loader/conversion/atlas/decoder files are covered (`image-image_rs.md`, `image-loader-atlas.md`); still open: the `PARENT: render` consumers (`GpuImage`/`RenderAsset<Image>` preparation, `fallback_image.hpp`, `screenshot.cpp`). `bevy_image/src/ktx2.rs` and `dds.rs` are enumerated at declaration level only (Epix has no counterpart for either file), and the unused surface of the pinned `rectangle-pack`/`guillotiere` crates is out of scope by design.
- **`pbr` (`PBR-`)** — beyond `render/mesh.rs` and the light set now covered by `pbr-lights.md`: `material.rs`, `material_bind_groups.rs`, the `mesh_bindings.rs` per-entry layout builders and the whole of `mesh_view_bindings.rs` (`MeshPipelineViewLayouts`, `MeshPipelineViewLayout`, `generate_view_layouts`, `layout_entries`, `MeshViewBindGroup`), `render/skin.rs`, `render/morph.rs`, `render/gpu_preprocess.rs` (`MeshPipelinePreprocess`, `preprocess`, `PreprocessPipelines`, `PreprocessBindGroups`, `IndirectParametersBuffers`), `lightmap/mod.rs`, `meshlet/**`, `deferred/**`, `ssr/**` and `volumetric_fog/**` against `epix_engine/pbr/**`.
- **`render/core_graph` (`CGR-`)** — the Bevy files both CGR blocks reference but do not own: `bevy_core_pipeline/src/prepass/node.rs` internals, `deferred/copy_lighting_id.rs` (CGR-200 is ⛔ for exactly that reason), `msaa_writeback.rs`, `bevy_render/src/view/mod.rs`, `bevy_camera/**`; and the Epix files outside the audited set (`core_graph/src/prepass.cpp`, `mip_generation.cpp`, `skybox.cpp`, `tonemapping.cpp`, `upscaling.cpp`, `blit.cpp`, `plugin.cpp` internals), which the rows cite only where they register or consume an audited label.
- **`color` (`COL-`, `CSL-`, `CSP-`, `COK-`, `COP-`)** — the port has no `color` module, so these five sections are a specification rather than a diff: they read seventeen `bevy_color` files in full (`color.rs`, `lib.rs`, `srgba.rs`, `linear_rgba.rs`, `hsla.rs`, `hsva.rs`, `hwba.rs`, `laba.rs`, `lcha.rs`, `xyza.rs`, `oklaba.rs`, `oklcha.rs`, `color_ops.rs`, `color_difference.rs`, `color_gradient.rs`, `color_range.rs`, `interpolate.rs`) and every row is 🚫 or ❌. Still to audit: the `palettes/**` module (820 lines — `basic.rs`, `css.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `mod.rs`), `testing.rs` and `test_colors.rs`. The first fix that waits on the module existing is `CAM-47` (`ClearColorConfig::Custom` holds a linear `ClearColor` and has no `From<Color>`), which cannot be resolved in the camera module alone.
- **Bevy subsystems with no Epix counterpart at all** — each is visible today only as ⛔/🚫 rows and needs a scope decision (port it, or record it as ⛔ with a rationale) before the module can be called aligned: atmosphere, decal/clustered decals, deferred materials, lightmap, meshlet, SSAO, SSR, volumetric fog, wireframe, picking (`bevy_picking`; all of SPR-424..SPR-435), order-independent transparency (CGR-571..CGR-593), render diagnostics (`pass_span`/`diagnostic_recorder`; CGR-208/218/226/294/301), the `bevy_solari` raytracing path, and asset reflection.

## Maintenance rules

- **A row's ID is stable.** `MSH-`/`IMG-`/`SPR-`/`SRD-`/`PBR-`/`CGR-`/`CAM-`/`COL-`/`CSL-`/`CSP-`/`COK-`/`COP-`/`PRT-` IDs are never reused, renumbered or deleted, and rows are never merged into one or dropped; an ID block, once allocated to a Bevy file, keeps its numbering, so a commit message, an approval request and a later re-audit all refer to the same mismatch.
- **A fixed row moves to ✅ with the fixing commit**, carrying the evidence the row needs: the focused module tests for logic-only/value-only changes, or a whole-tree build plus the full CTest sweep plus the example sweep on both output streams plus stable client-area captures for anything that can affect rendering (see `_policy.md`, "Verification policy").
- **The Audit index counts are recomputed, never hand-edited.** Adding or merging a section means re-parsing the row tables under `tmp/audit/sections/**` and recomputing every count; where a section's prose summary disagrees with its own rows, the computed number wins and the disagreement is recorded as a footnote under the index (see the `mesh-lead-verified.md` footnote).
- **A section file may only be merged into this file verbatim.** The files under `tmp/audit/sections/` are the working papers — they may be edited, split or superseded — while this file is the record: `## Audited sections` reproduces each one under its `<!-- section: … -->` marker without rewriting, renumbering, reordering or summarising a single row, and a correction is made in the section file and re-merged rather than patched here.
- **Every non-✅ row appears in the Open mismatch index, and every non-✅ `PARENT:`/`PRT-` row in the parent-module table** — a `PARENT:` marker counts wherever the section puts it, in the difference cell or in the Entity/Epix cell, so a divergence recorded only on the entity is not missed; the ✅ rows a section marked `PARENT:` in the difference cell stay in the table as coverage evidence. A new section must extend both tables; a row that reaches ✅ leaves the Open mismatch index and stays in the merged section as coverage evidence.
- **A parent-module fix is approved before committing** (`render`, `app`, `ecs`, `assets`, `camera`, `transform`, …): the mismatch IDs, the changed files and the evidence go to the user first, and a parent module that turns out to diverge is audited again rather than patched around.
- **A new section file is merged verbatim; only the counts and the two index tables are recomputed.** Adding a section appends its file under `## Audited sections` behind a `<!-- section: … -->` marker in the declared order, then re-derives the Audit index counts, the Open mismatch index and the parent-module table from the parsed rows; the hand-written prose, the fix batches and the already-merged sections are copied unchanged.
